title: throttle investigator canvas notes
collaborators: Jordan Kim, Luis Herrera, Sofia Becker
tags: rate-limits, quotas, usage-analytics, ux, wireframe, per-identity
content:
Purpose: notes and sketch ideas for a unified console canvas that helps operators trace, simulate, and remediate throttling incidents across identities (api key, org, route, model). This is a working doc with rough sketches, telemetry suggestions, and an initial backlog.

Problem summary:
- Customers repeatedly ask why a single route produced 429s while other routes remained healthy.
- Ops want quick narrow fixes (temporary quota bump, route exception, model fallback) with cost visibility.
- Current console separates quotas, rate limits, and usage analytics; users must context-switch.
- Need an integrated per-identity exploration surface that is both investigatory and actionable.

Design principles:
1) Keep identity and time window pinned while changing other filters.
2) Make actions proximal: simulate or preview from every data surface.
3) Be cost-aware: estimate token and dollar impact of changes.
4) Distinguish failure modes: throttles, errors, degraded fallbacks.
5) Provide lightweight simulations that are clearly labelled as estimates.

Top user journeys:
- Investigate spike: select an api key, surface which routes and models spiked, identify the route and time window, simulate a temporary quota bump, apply if safe.
- Capacity planning: org-level 30d burn-down by route, recommendations for reserved capacity or autoscale.
- Incident triage: search for 429s in a timeframe, get likely cause (burst, sustained, bug) and suggested mitigations.

Layout (left-to-right):
- Top bar: identity selector (api key | org | service account), time window picker (quick presets + custom), environment toggle (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Metrics row: usage percent, throttled request count, peak rps, estimated next-hour cost at current burn rate.
- Main region split 60/40: left is exploration canvas with tabs (overview, routes, models, heatmap, raw events); right is the action pane with recommendations, simulation, recent quota changes, audit preview, and one-click override when permitted.

ASCII sketch:
[Top bar: Identity: (API Key v)  Time: (Last 1h v)  Env: hosted]
[Metrics: Usage 74% | 429s 532 | Peak 812 rps | est/hr $22]
|---------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Left canvas (tabs)        | Right action pane             |
| Overview                  | Recommendations               |
| - burn-down sparkline     | - likely cause: route /chat   |
| - top routes table        | - suggested delta: +20%       |
| Routes tab                | Simulation panel              |
| - stacked timeline        | - apply for 1h preview        |
| Heatmap (route x hour)    | Audit trail                   |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------|

Exploration surfaces:
- Overview: 30d burn-down sparkline, top 10 routes by volume, top 5 api keys by burn rate, auto-generated summary line.
- Routes tab: per-route stacked timeline showing success vs throttled vs errors. Route row drilldown shows model breakdown and response size distribution.
- Heatmap: rows are routes, columns are hourly buckets, color encodes throttled rate. Hover reveals counts, percentage throttled, and sample failed request ids when authorized.
- Raw events: stream view with search, copyable request id, timestamp, route, key, and response code for SRE debugging.
- Simulation pane: fields for new quota value, window type, scope (single key / org / route override), and duration. Shows predicted throttles avoided and cost delta estimate.

Recommendations heuristics (proposal):
- If throttled count exceeds threshold and is sustained, recommend a percentage bump or model fallback.
- If a single key accounts for more than half the org burn, recommend per-key cap or separate service account.
- If route token length variance is high, recommend a burst window instead of sustained quota.
Each recommendation should include rationale, confidence level, impacted identities, and a simulate button.

Telemetry suggestions:
- UI events: page_view.usage_canvas, click.simulate_quota, click.apply_override, export.csv, toggle.env. Include identity id and user id in payloads.
- Backend events: quota_usage with key, org, route, window; throttle_events with key, route, reason; simulated_change_preview with key, delta, duration, estimated_throttles_avoided, estimated_cost_delta.
- Important log fields: request_id, api_key_id, org_id, route_name, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, response_code, latency_ms, throttled_bool, quota_window.

Sample analytics query (example):
SELECT route_name, SUM(throttled) as throttled_count, SUM(tokens_in + tokens_out) as tokens FROM events WHERE api_key_id = 'ak_12345' AND ts > now() - interval '6 hours' GROUP BY route_name ORDER BY throttled_count DESC LIMIT 20;

MVP acceptance criteria:
- Filter by identity and time window and show a burn-down sparkline and top 10 routes.
- Clicking a route opens a detail modal with per-hour throttled percent and sample request ids for authorized users.
- Simulation computes a deterministic estimate for throttles avoided and approximate cost delta within a stated tolerance (e.g., +/- 25%).
- Audit log links to recent quota changes and respects RBAC; only users with quota.modify see apply actions.
- Support CSV export of the current table and heatmap snapshot.

Backlog priorities:
P0 (MVP): identity/time picker, burn-down sparkline, top routes table, route modal, simulation panel with linear estimator, telemetry hooks.
P1: heatmap with hover tooltips, rule-based recommendations engine, RBAC gates and audit-history retrieval.
P2: cost forecasting with model mix, autosuggest rate-limit rules, integration with Dedicated autoscale controls.

Open questions and edge cases:
- Historical data for deleted api keys: display read-only history but disable simulate/apply.
- Mixed environments: how to present combined burn-down across hosted and private deployments; likely read-only combined view with links.
- Simulation accuracy when workload characteristics shift; consider a conservative safety factor.
- Who sets default recommendation thresholds: product defaults or org-level config?

Permissions and security:
- Only users with quota.modify can apply overrides. Simulation allowed for read-only users.
- Audit entries must capture actor, reason text, duration, and pre-change quota snapshot.

Microcopy guidance:
- Use plain language for recommendations and include an info icon explaining estimate methodology.

Rollout plan overview:
- Week 0: feature flag work, backend endpoints, telemetry.
- Week 1: deliver identity selector, burn-down and top routes table.
- Week 2: add heatmap, route modal, and simulation. Beta release to select customers.
- Week 3+: gather feedback, refine heuristics, and enable progressive rollout of recommendations.

Requests for teams:
- Engineering: confirm feasibility of surfacing per-request throttled boolean in analytics.
- Data: validate the linear estimator and its error bounds against historical traffic.
- Legal: review export of request ids for compliance with retention and privacy rules.

Reviewer notes: this doc aims to unify exploration and action. Feedback requested on what signals should appear in the right-hand action pane and the expected fidelity of the simulation.

Next steps and TODOs:
- Conduct two customer interviews focused on ops workflows.
- Prototype the heatmap and simulation in Figma.
- Open telemetry tickets for the UI and backend events listed above.

End of notes.
